It's good, but I don't like it. It's just too generic (I'm aware of the irony) and needs a better hook. Maybe if it's small-talk had random "WTF?" moments.
Along the lines of, "Hey Joe, working hard or hardly working? How's the wife and kids? Boy that boss-man is really riding me today, I'm going to eat one of his kidneys. Did you see that new girl in accounting?"

6 years later edit: I don't know if it's because of interim re-writes or change in my tastes, but I like this now.
I read 600's last line of dialogue not as after the fact censorship, but as him actually saying out loud "..open brackets redacted close brackets…" Which may have scratched the itch I had when commenting originally back in 2012.

There is something about this rewrite that has struck a real "Oh my god" chord with me.

That feeling of wanting to reach out and connect with someone, but being unable to do so. I mean, what this does is kind of the opposite of what I do (I'm terrible at small talk), but the effects feel the same somehow.

It won't hit everyone the same way, but this has my vote and it's going to stick with me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Hmm… well, if its very existence depends on being liked (in a manner of speaking), then I think it would be a little bit more desperate for human contact. If someone were to conduct an interview with it and leave it alone in a room, for instance, I think it would then try very hard to get the interviewer to stay. If left alone, I think it wouldn't just kind of sit there at first, but, like— bang on walls or something for a while. Then after a while its "fuel" of being liked would run out and it would shamble over to the center of the room and kind of sit there until someone else came in. At least that's my idea of how a thing like this would work.

Okay: much better than the last version, but I'm not seeing a hook yet. Does this thing have an agenda, or does it simply exist? If it simply exists, it doesn't do enough tricks for an upvote quite yet. Perhaps you could add a single incident implying at some hidden motivation of this thing. I'm sort of sensing a hook around the "refers to itself in 3rd person" bit, but it's just not enough for me to grab onto.

Once again I will refrain from voting, but this SCP is definitely on the right track. I love the fact that it's featureless and self-sustaining, it just needs to do something cool before I click that + button.
